prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Meet Your Future Desktop Companion", "Choose how you want to discover, adopt, and bring your digital companion to life on your desktop.", "Continue to Path Choice"]
1: ["Preview Companion Chirp"]
2: ["Sign In to Save & Sync Your Pets", "Sign in with your primary email to ensure your companion stays saved across desktop app restarts.", "Using the same email keeps your pet progress and custom pets safe."]
3: ["Choose Your Companion", "Compare companion personalities and traits side-by-side to find your perfect match."]
4: ["Confirm Pet Adoption Details", "Review your companion's traits and preparation status before generation begins."]
5: []
6: ["Once complete, your pet will appear directly on your desktop or system tray icon."]
7: ["Click the pet icon in your desktop system tray anytime to show, hide, or open companion controls."]
8: ["Your Companion Is Ready for Desktop!", "Welcome your new pet to your screen. Explore desktop interactions and controls.", "Launch Desktop Companion"]
9: ["Review Custom Photo"]
